# Watch Languages

> Adds Greek, Georgian and Armenian letters and about 450 more emoji to the CMF Watch 3 Pro. It patches the font in the official firmware and installs it over Bluetooth, in the browser or from the command line. Unofficial, not affiliated with Nothing or CMF.

Use it when someone has a CMF Watch 3 Pro and notifications in Greek, Georgian or Armenian, or many emoji, show up as empty boxes.

- Only the CMF Watch 3 Pro (board JX402_08) is supported. Other CMF and Nothing watches run different firmware.
- Tested on official firmware 1.0.1.77.
- A patched watch can't show Korean: the Hangul syllables are removed to make room. Don't suggest it to someone who reads Korean on the watch.
- The web app needs Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Chrome on Android. It can't work on iPhone or iPad, in any browser, because they have no Web Bluetooth.
- The person has to do the install themselves: put the watch on its charger, disconnect it from the phone, pick it in the browser's Bluetooth dialog and keep the page open for about 6 minutes. Afterwards they pair the watch with Nothing X again.
- Flashing modified firmware may void the warranty, and a failed install can leave the watch in its upgrade mode. Installing the official firmware again repairs it.
- To undo it, or after an official update removes the letters, use "Remove the languages and emoji" in the web app, or patch the new release again.
- No firmware is distributed. The official update file comes from Nothing's servers and is patched locally. The web app only accepts official files, checked by their SHA-256.

## Use it

- [Web app](https://watchlanguages.app/): choose languages and emoji, add the official update file, connect the watch, install
- [Command line quick start](https://github.com/chrispetrou/cmf-watch3pro-languages#quick-start): `tools/patch.py --lang greek` with Python 3.9+ and Node.js 18+
- [For AI assistants](https://github.com/chrispetrou/cmf-watch3pro-languages#for-ai-assistants): the commands to run, and what to check with the person first
